A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FLARE research. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable matching across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original FLARE evaluations on XNLI, TyDiQA, and NusaX, including ablations, translation-quality comparisons, and activation analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds a manual error analysis and statistical comparisons.

M1.justification: FLARE's LoRA bottleneck fusion, fusion functions, training procedure, and FLARE MT projection remain unchanged. Expanded explanations and the relocated FLARE MT schematic do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: The datasets, languages, tasks, and translation scenarios remain unchanged, including the appendix experiments using gold translations and training-only fusion. The new error analysis samples existing TyDiQA coverage.

E2.justification: The same zero-shot, translate-test, LoRA, X-Mixup, and input-level fusion comparisons remain, including the appendix comparisons. Adding X-Mixup citations to Table 1 does not add a comparator.

E3.justification: v2 adds average-rank reporting in Table 1 and a manual inspection protocol involving 200 randomly selected TyDiQA examples with Llama 3.1 and Gemma 2. Existing benchmark splits, task metrics, model configurations, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 8 adds a targeted manual error analysis asking whether translation quality explains TyDiQA failures. The existing fusion-function, adapter-capacity, translation-quality, activation, and training-only-fusion analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v1 reports means and standard deviations over five seeds. v2 adds systematic Pitman permutation tests across all three datasets, four model families, both FLARE variants, and three baselines in Table 9, substantially extending statistical assessment. Five seeds were already documented in v1 Appendix B; the revised Table 1 caption does not establish additional runs.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes Llama 3.1 translate-test XNLI accuracy from 79.43 to 79.08, matching the unchanged Table 6, and adds average ranks. v2 also adds p-values and reports no translation-attributed errors in its manual audit. Per-language benchmark scores in Tables 6–8 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The fusion equations and mathematical assumptions are retained, with no new proofs or derivations. Changing r ≪ h to r ≪ d in Section 3.3 corrects the dimensional notation without revising the underlying reasoning.

C1.justification: The core contributions and claims about efficient representation fusion, architectural flexibility, and multilingual QA benefits remain unchanged. The headline 4.9- and 2.2-point TyDiQA improvements are retained; describing them as absolute in the introduction clarifies the existing results.

C2.justification: Section 8 expands the translation-availability limitation to translation quality and cultural preservation in extremely low-resource languages, and suggests incorporating cultural context through fusion. Appendix A newly interprets the permutation tests as supporting consistent, often significant improvements, overgeneralizing some FLARE MT comparisons.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 now explicitly explains the existing LoRA rank and how alpha scales low-rank updates before addition to frozen outputs. Hyperparameter values, precision and compute disclosures, implementation information in Appendices B–D, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Alemayehu et al. (2024) to support translation-error limitations and cites the already-discussed Qu et al. (2025) alongside the fusion expression. The broader related-work framing and novelty positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: Limited edits clarify translation directions, task-specific fine-tuning, baseline selection, and LoRA parameters, alongside wording and model-name corrections. The overall narrative and section structure are retained.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains an average-rank column and caption details, and v2 adds the significance-test Table 9. The existing FLARE MT schematic moves from appendix Figure 7 to main-text Figure 3. Other figures are renumbered, some appendix averages gain bold emphasis, and the dataset overview becomes Table 10.

improvement.justification: The significance table, targeted error analysis, clearer limitations, and corrected Table 1 entry modestly improve transparency. These gains are limited by overstated statistical interpretation: Appendix A describes improvements although Llama TyDiQA FLARE MT scores 38.95 versus LoRA's 42.84 with p = 0.029. The added evidence remains useful, while the method and primary benchmark findings are essentially unchanged.
